 HONOLULU – The University of Hawaii men's basketball team enjoyed a record-breaking night in a 116-44 rout of Bethesda on the opening evening of the 60th Annual OUTRIGGER Rainbow Classic Friday at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center. 
UH's 72-point win set a new record for largest margin of victory in program history, eclipsing the previous mark of 67 points, set in a 110-43 win over BYU Hawaii on Nov. 20, 1962.
The 116 points was also the fourth-highest total in program history and highest since UH scored 117 against Memphis State on March 2, 1974. 
It was also a milestone evening for head coach Eran Ganot , who claimed his 200th career victory with the emphatic result. A total of 197 of the wins have come at Hawaii, while the other three occurred when he served as acting coach at Saint Mary's, prior to his tenure at UH.
All 11 players who suited up got in the scoring column, including seven in double-figures.
 Zack Davidson led the 'Bows with 20 points on 9-of-12 shooting from the field, while adding 10 rebounds for a double-double. Chance Trujillo hit four of UH's 12 three-pointers and finished with 14 points. Tanner Cuff also scored 14 points and Kellen Hampton added 13. Bol Dengdit posted a double-double with 12 points and a game-high 12 rebounds. Marcus Adams Jr. also finished with 12 points and Jaden Mantingou had 10 points. 
 Tiger Cuff dished out a game-high seven assists and Lueth Awan contributed nine points and nine rebounds off the bench.
 Coast to coast @kingcuff1 🤯 📺 K5/MW+ #GoBows https://t.co/n5XNV987Om
— HAWAII BASKETBALL (@HawaiiMBB) November 7, 2026 
UH spotted the Lion Angels the first three points of the game and was behind 5-3 before the 'Bows went on an 8-0 run to take the lead. It was a lead they wouldn't relinquish the rest of the evening. UH took its first double-digit lead midway through the first half, then out-scored the Lion Angels by 29 points in the final minutes to take a commanding 61-21 lead at the break. 
UH shot 58 percent in the first half and held Bethesda to just 29 percent shooting. 
UH continued to add to the margin in the second half and hit triple digits when Awan drained a three-pointer with 7:15 left to secure the 43rd 100-point game in program history. The lead grew to 70 with 4:07 left on the way to the record margin.
 Both ends for @KellenHampton 💪🏽 📺 K5/MW+ #ManaOhana x #GoBows https://t.co/yePnjgQ3cC
— HAWAII BASKETBALL (@HawaiiMBB) November 7, 2026 
The 'Bows finished at 53.6 percent shooting to Bethesda's 26.3 percent and scored 60 points in the paint. UH's 62 rebounds marked the highest total since grabbing 70 against Redlands on Jan. 28, 1972. 
In the first game of the evening, UT Arlington defeated Portland, 89-85.
The Rainbow Classic continues on Sunday with Portland vs. Bethesda at 2:30 p.m., followed by Hawaii vs. UT Arlington at 5:00 p.m.
